title: Becoming states
hook: Acquisition and admission are different dates.
notes: Original Orbis factual synthesis; linked federal records and historic-site accounts, checked 14 October 2026. Points locate places approximately, not territorial extents. Modern national/state outlines are reference geography, never reconstructed historical borders. No archival images or source prose redistributed. Sources by scene: Ratifying the original union: https://www.senate.gov/states/DE/intro.htm; California: admission after acquisition: https://www.senate.gov/states/CA/intro.htm; Alaska: purchase, territory, state: https://www.senate.gov/states/AK/intro.htm; Hawaii: the fiftieth state: https://www.senate.gov/states/HI/intro.htm

scenes.title: Ratifying the original union
scenes.text: Delaware ratified the Constitution in 1787. Its position as the first state reflects ratification order; the state already existed before that constitutional decision.

scenes.title: California: admission after acquisition
scenes.text: California became a state in 1850, after the Mexican cession of 1848. Admission brought representation in the federal union rather than a new international acquisition.

scenes.title: Alaska: purchase, territory, state
scenes.text: Alaska joined the union in January 1959. The gap from the 1867 purchase shows why an acquisition map and a statehood map answer different questions.

scenes.title: Hawaii: the fiftieth state
scenes.text: Hawaii became a state in August 1959. Its island geography places part of the union far beyond the contiguous mainland.
